rowDispositions.currentMeaning: Boundary-focused design that trusts internal traffic more than external traffic; common in older network models.
rowDispositions.priorReason: HOLD: the full category is defined as trusting internal traffic more; boundary protections can coexist with resource-based Zero Trust without implicit internal trust.

rowDispositions.currentMeaning: Security model based on never trust, always verify with continuous checks for users, devices, and sessions.
rowDispositions.priorReason: HOLD: never-trust/always-verify plus continuous checks does not state resource access authorization or removal of implicit trust based on network location/ownership.

rowDispositions.currentMeaning: Cloud infrastructure owned by a third-party provider and accessed over the internet.
rowDispositions.priorReason: HOLD: the definition omits provisioning for open use by the general public; ownership and access path are insufficient distinguishing criteria.

rowDispositions.currentMeaning: Environment that connects private cloud or on-premises resources with public cloud services.
rowDispositions.priorReason: HOLD: ordinary on-premises resources plus public services do not necessarily form distinct cloud infrastructures bound for data/application portability.

rowDispositions.currentMeaning: Replacing sensitive data with a token that has no useful value outside the token vault.
rowDispositions.priorReason: HOLD new: no useful value outside the vault conflates inability to recover the original value with legitimate application/payment utility. A vault example does not establish universal harmlessness, authorization or attacker uselessness.

rowDispositions.currentMeaning: Irreversibly removing identifying links so individuals cannot be re-identified.
rowDispositions.priorReason: HOLD new: irreversible removal of explicit links does not establish an absolute cannot-be-reidentified outcome with auxiliary data and quasi-identifiers. Distinguish the intended anonymization goal from a demonstrated privacy result.

rowDispositions.currentMeaning: Spreading systems across regions so one local disaster does not take down the whole service.
rowDispositions.priorReason: HOLD: across-region placement alone does not ensure one local disaster cannot take down the whole service. Shared dependencies, data/traffic failover, capacity and independent operability remain unspecified; the outcome is overstated rather than expressed as a risk-reduction goal.

rowDispositions.currentMeaning: Documented step-by-step procedure analysts follow during repeatable incident response tasks.
rowDispositions.priorReason: HOLD: one step-by-step incident-task definition supplies no component distinction or relationship for Playbook versus Runbook.

rowDispositions.currentMeaning: Using controls such as hashing to prove logs were not altered, deleted, or tampered with.
rowDispositions.priorReason: HOLD: controls such as hashing are described as proving logs were not altered, deleted or tampered with without a protected baseline or completeness evidence.

rowDispositions.currentMeaning: Third party that processes personal data on behalf of a data controller.
rowDispositions.priorReason: HOLD: the authored card calls a processor a Third party. Colloquial external-provider usage is understandable, but GDPR Article4(10), as explained by EDPB paragraphs86-89, excludes the processor from third party in that same processing relationship.

rowDispositions.currentMeaning: Technical role that maintains data and implements controls such as storage, backups, access, and retention.
rowDispositions.priorReason: HOLD: one combined label supplies only technical storage/backup/access/retention work; it does not distinguish the lesson steward quality/governance coordination from custodian implementation.

rowDispositions.currentMeaning: Risk analysis that uses descriptive ratings such as high, medium, low, or a numbered risk matrix.
rowDispositions.priorReason: HOLD: an unspecified numbered risk matrix is not necessarily qualitative. Ordinal category codes, semi-quantitative scores and measured quantitative values differ; the card omits the distinction needed to classify them.

rowDispositions.currentMeaning: Acceptable variation from the organization's risk appetite for a specific situation or system.
rowDispositions.priorReason: HOLD: acceptable variation from risk appetite uses the wrong or ambiguous reference point. Tolerance describes acceptable risk/performance bounds for objectives in context, aligned with appetite; it is not blanket permission to vary outside appetite. The actual objective/threshold basis is missing.

rowDispositions.expansionObserved: Bring Your Own Device / Corporate-Owned Personally Enabled / Choose Your Own Device
rowDispositions.currentMeaning: Mobile-device ownership models with different security and privacy tradeoffs.
rowDispositions.priorReason: HOLD: the meaning only announces different security/privacy tradeoffs; it does not distinguish personally owned work devices, corporate-owned personally enabled devices, or selection from an approved device catalogue.

rowDispositions.expansionObserved: Infrastructure / Platform / Software as a Service
rowDispositions.currentMeaning: Cloud service models with different responsibility split between customer and provider.
rowDispositions.priorReason: HOLD: different responsibility split supplies no individual service capability or customer/provider control boundary for IaaS, PaaS and SaaS.

rowDispositions.currentMeaning: Unique hardware address assigned to a network interface.
rowDispositions.priorReason: HOLD: calling every MAC a unique hardware address overstates permanent physical-device identity; the existing support identity also collides with Mandatory Access Control.

localDrafts.priorReason: HOLD: the full category is defined as trusting internal traffic more; boundary protections can coexist with resource-based Zero Trust without implicit internal trust.

replacement.meaning: In network architecture, controls that inspect or restrict traffic at defined boundaries. They can coexist with resource-focused authorization without automatically trusting internal traffic.

localDrafts.contextNote: Network-boundary context only; no guarantee that perimeter controls alone authorize access or prevent compromise.

sourceReferences.claimScope: Abstract: resource focus, no location/ownership-only implicit trust, distinct authentication/authorization.

localDrafts.priorReason: HOLD: never-trust/always-verify plus continuous checks does not state resource access authorization or removal of implicit trust based on network location/ownership.

replacement.meaning: Architecture that protects resources through explicit authentication and authorization, without granting implicit trust solely because of network location or device ownership.

localDrafts.contextNote: Reuse the bounded ZTA glossary candidate text, with a new exact card binding. The glossary hold and canonical mapping remain separate and unresolved.

sourceReferences.claimScope: Abstract: resource focus, no location/ownership-only implicit trust, distinct authentication/authorization.

localDrafts.priorReason: HOLD: the definition omits provisioning for open use by the general public; ownership and access path are insufficient distinguishing criteria.

replacement.meaning: Cloud infrastructure offered for use by the general public. Provider ownership or internet connectivity alone does not define this deployment model.

localDrafts.contextNote: Public availability of the service does not mean every workload or customer dataset is publicly accessible.

sourceReferences.claimScope: Section2 service/deployment definitions; bounded capability/control distinctions, not modern service conformance.

localDrafts.priorReason: HOLD: ordinary on-premises resources plus public services do not necessarily form distinct cloud infrastructures bound for data/application portability.

replacement.meaning: Two or more distinct private, community or public cloud infrastructures that retain their identities and are connected to enable data or application portability.

localDrafts.contextNote: An ordinary on-premises server plus an internet service is not sufficient; private/community composition need not contain public cloud.

sourceReferences.claimScope: Section2 service/deployment definitions; bounded capability/control distinctions, not modern service conformance.

localDrafts.priorReason: HOLD new: no useful value outside the vault conflates inability to recover the original value with legitimate application/payment utility. A vault example does not establish universal harmlessness, authorization or attacker uselessness.

replacement.meaning: Replacing sensitive data with substitute tokens to reduce exposure of the original data. Tokens can still support authorized processing; protection depends on design, allowed use and access to mapping or detokenization functions.

localDrafts.contextNote: A vault is one implementation pattern, not a guarantee that every token is harmless, unusable or recoverable only through that pattern. No current PCI compliance claim.

sourceReferences.claimScope: Historical2011 section2.2 approved applications/tokenization requests; example and design dependence, not current PCI requirements.

localDrafts.priorReason: HOLD new: irreversible removal of explicit links does not establish an absolute cannot-be-reidentified outcome with auxiliary data and quasi-identifiers. Distinguish the intended anonymization goal from a demonstrated privacy result.

replacement.meaning: Transforming data with the aim that people are no longer identifiable. Whether that result is achieved depends on remaining identifiers, available linking information and assessed re-identification risk.

localDrafts.contextNote: Deleting names alone does not demonstrate anonymization. This describes the privacy goal and need for assessment, not a legal anonymity finding or an achieved irreversible result.

sourceReferences.claimScope: Section2.2 terminology and targeted linkage/threat-model passages; privacy goal versus assessed re-identification risk.

localDrafts.priorReason: HOLD: across-region placement alone does not ensure one local disaster cannot take down the whole service. Shared dependencies, data/traffic failover, capacity and independent operability remain unspecified; the outcome is overstated rather than expressed as a risk-reduction goal.

replacement.meaning: Distributing systems across separated locations to reduce exposure to a single local event. Continued service also depends on controlling common failure dependencies, usable capacity, data availability and tested failover.

localDrafts.contextNote: Separated sites may still share DNS, identity, control or other failure dependencies. Placement is not an achieved RTO/RPO or service-continuity guarantee.

sourceReferences.claimScope: Multi-location dependencies and independence limits; vendor example, not an operational recovery test.

localDrafts.priorReason: HOLD: one step-by-step incident-task definition supplies no component distinction or relationship for Playbook versus Runbook.

replacement.meaning: In a common study convention, a playbook sets incident-response guidance, decisions and roles; a runbook gives detailed steps for a specific task. Organizations may combine these or use the names differently.

localDrafts.contextNote: This is a declared terminology convention, not a universal hierarchy or a human-versus-automation distinction. The compound card does not create two assessed skills.

sourceReferences.claimScope: Vendor runbook as ordered task actions; no universal playbook/runbook hierarchy. CISA playbook search excerpt only; fresh CISA page/PDF retrieval unavailable.

localDrafts.priorReason: HOLD: controls such as hashing are described as proving logs were not altered, deleted or tampered with without a protected baseline or completeness evidence.

replacement.meaning: Protecting logs against unauthorized changes and detecting alteration using controls such as restricted access and comparisons with protected integrity baselines. A hash alone does not prove logs are complete or undeleted.

localDrafts.contextNote: A replaceable baseline can match altered content, and a valid surviving record hash does not reveal missing records. These are reviewer counterexamples, not a deployed logging assessment.

sourceReferences.claimScope: Legacy final log-management abstract only. PDF text-find unavailable; protected-baseline/completeness limits are explicit reviewer inferences and synthetic checks.

localDrafts.priorReason: HOLD: the authored card calls a processor a Third party. Colloquial external-provider usage is understandable, but GDPR Article4(10), as explained by EDPB paragraphs86-89, excludes the processor from third party in that same processing relationship.

replacement.meaning: In GDPR, a person or body processing personal data on a controller's behalf and instructions. The controller determines the purposes and means of processing.

localDrafts.contextNote: Use the processing relationship rather than an informal third-party label. Actual legal roles depend on the activity; no contract, organisation or individual is classified.

sourceReferences.claimScope: Controller purpose/means versus processor acting on behalf/instructions. No legal applicability finding.

localDrafts.priorReason: HOLD: one combined label supplies only technical storage/backup/access/retention work; it does not distinguish the lesson steward quality/governance coordination from custodian implementation.

replacement.meaning: A custodian implements technical storage, access and lifecycle controls. A steward coordinates data definitions, quality and governance with business users and the data owner. Organizations can combine or name these roles differently.

localDrafts.contextNote: A bounded study distinction consistent with the referenced government model, not universal job descriptions or a canonical split of this compound identity.

sourceReferences.claimScope: Steward and custodian sections; context-specific coordination/quality versus technical implementation example.

localDrafts.priorReason: HOLD: an unspecified numbered risk matrix is not necessarily qualitative. Ordinal category codes, semi-quantitative scores and measured quantitative values differ; the card omits the distinction needed to classify them.

replacement.meaning: Assessing risk with defined categories such as Low, Medium and High. A numbered matrix must be interpreted: category labels, semi-quantitative scores and measured quantities are different kinds of values.

localDrafts.contextNote: Numbers alone do not determine the assessment type or justify arithmetic on ordinal labels; the scale, rules and uncertainty need context.

sourceReferences.claimScope: Section2.3 assessment approaches: qualitative categories versus semi-quantitative scales and quantitative measures.

localDrafts.priorReason: HOLD: acceptable variation from risk appetite uses the wrong or ambiguous reference point. Tolerance describes acceptable risk/performance bounds for objectives in context, aligned with appetite; it is not blanket permission to vary outside appetite. The actual objective/threshold basis is missing.

replacement.meaning: Specific acceptable risk or performance bounds for a stated objective, used to guide decisions and aligned with the organization's risk appetite.

localDrafts.contextNote: Definitions vary by source/context. Tolerance is not blanket permission to exceed appetite, a measured risk result or an actual acceptance decision.

sourceReferences.claimScope: Multiple context-bound definitions: acceptable risk or objective-relative performance bounds; no universal formula.

localDrafts.priorReason: HOLD: the meaning only announces different security/privacy tradeoffs; it does not distinguish personally owned work devices, corporate-owned personally enabled devices, or selection from an approved device catalogue.

replacement.meaning: BYOD uses personally owned devices for work. COPE uses organization-owned devices with permitted personal use. CYOD offers an approved device list; ownership and funding depend on the organization's policy.

localDrafts.contextNote: Distinguish ownership, permitted use and approved-list choice rather than treating all three as ownership categories. The current CYOD glossary and its offline candidate remain independent.

sourceReferences.claimScope: Earlier bound section5.1.3 CYOD evidence retained; final landing page reread, fresh PDF retrieval unavailable. No full mobile-policy audit.

localDrafts.priorReason: HOLD: different responsibility split supplies no individual service capability or customer/provider control boundary for IaaS, PaaS and SaaS.

replacement.meaning: IaaS provides processing, storage and networking while customers control their operating systems and applications. PaaS provides a managed platform for customer-deployed applications. SaaS provides provider-run applications. Customer access, data and configuration responsibilities still depend on the service and agreement.

localDrafts.contextNote: These are introductory service capabilities/control boundaries, not a complete security responsibility matrix or a claim that SaaS removes all customer duties.

sourceReferences.claimScope: Section2 service/deployment definitions; bounded capability/control distinctions, not modern service conformance.

localDrafts.priorReason: HOLD: calling every MAC a unique hardware address overstates permanent physical-device identity; the existing support identity also collides with Mandatory Access Control.

replacement.meaning: Address used by a network interface at the link layer. It may be assigned locally or randomized, so it is not reliable proof of a unique physical device. Here MAC refers to media access control.

localDrafts.contextNote: Mandatory Access Control is a different meaning of MAC. Correcting this text does not repair the shared support-node identity, approve a node split or change any glossary/card alias.

sourceReferences.claimScope: Private/rotating Wi-Fi MAC addresses as a counterexample to fixed hardware identity; no device configuration performed.
